standard_prerequisites: The zero scheme of a nonzero global section of an invertible sheaf and the divisor of a section, together with the order of vanishing of a section along a prime divisor
Elementary etale neighbourhoods and the identification of the henselizations of the local rings of a point and of the corresponding point of the neighbourhood
Flat base change of lengths along the map from a local ring to its henselization, and the identification of the coefficients of a cycle by comparing them at generic points
core_obligations: Fix an integral closed subspace of dimension one less than the ambient space and its generic point, and reduce the first equality to the comparison of the coefficient of that subspace on both sides
Choose an elementary etale neighbourhood of the generic point and shrink it so that the invertible sheaf is trivialised, and write the section there as a function times the trivialising section

Identify the pullback of the zero scheme to that neighbourhood as the zero scheme of the function, so that the coefficient of the subspace in the cycle of the zero scheme is a length of a quotient of the local ring
Compare that length with the corresponding length over the henselization, using flatness and the identification of residue fields
Recognise the resulting expression as the order of vanishing of the section along the subspace, which is its coefficient in the divisor, and thereby obtain both equalities
proof_roadmap: Reduce to the comparison of one coefficient at the generic point of an integral closed subspace of the critical dimension
Choose an elementary etale neighbourhood and trivialise the sheaf to reduce the zero scheme to the zero scheme of a function
Match the two length expressions through the henselization and read off the order of vanishing
difficulty_reason: The counted conclusion is the identification of the divisor of a nonzero global section with the class of its zero scheme and with the first Chern class cap at source lines 2327-2342, label lemma-compute-c1, whose proof occupies source lines 2344-2382. The proof is a coefficient comparison that has to move to a neighbourhood where the invertible sheaf becomes trivial: it chooses an elementary etale neighbourhood of the generic point of an integral closed subspace of the critical dimension, identifies the pullback of the zero scheme with the zero scheme of the local equation of the section, and then compares a length of a quotient of the local ring with the corresponding length over the henselization, using flatness and the identification of residue fields, before recognising the result as the order of vanishing. The counted statement records neither the neighbourhood nor the length comparison.
